entities.summary: Applied science emerged in the 18th century as a discipline that applies existing scientific knowledge to develop more practical applications, transforming the way people approached innovation and problem-solving. The development of applied science was influenced by the work of pioneers such as Benjamin Franklin, who experimented with electricity and developed practical uses for it. The field also drew on the work of scientists like Antoine Lavoisier, who developed methods for analyzing and quantifying chemical compounds. As applied science continued to evolve, it had significant regional impacts, particularly in the United Kingdom and the United States, where it contributed to the development of modern industries such as textiles, manufacturing, and transportation. The legacy of applied science can be seen in the many inventions and innovations that have transformed modern life, from the steam engine to the internet. The discipline has also had a profound impact on the way people think about science and its role in society, influencing the development of the scientific method and the importance of experimentation and empirical evidence. In the 20th century, applied science continued to evolve, with the rise of new technologies and fields such as computer science and biotechnology. Today, applied science remains a vital part of modern society, with its principles and methods being applied in a wide range of fields, from medicine and engineering to economics and environmental science.
